links.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy with vs without AI invasive-lesion prompts
links.effect: Reader study (3 pathologists, n=137 WSIs): accuracy gains 11.7%, 28.5%, 28.5%; panel AUC 0.616 to 0.921. Prospective 70 patients: 82.86% manual vs 92.9% with AI; 5 surgical approaches modified.
links.quote: The analysis revealed that HSFLA improved the pathologists’ diagnostic AUC from 0.616 to 0.921.

links.outcome: Performance on external second-center test set vs internal test set
links.effect: HSFLA accuracy 95.62% internal vs 91.7% external (AUC 98.71% vs 94.2%); weakly supervised methods dropped more substantially.
links.quote: In the three-classification task, it achieved a classification accuracy of 91.7% and an AUC of 94.2%.

links.outcome: Registration failure due to tissue damage/fragmentation in consecutive slides
links.effect: 2.6% of WSIs failed registration (Dice <75%); tissue tearing caused 3D reconstruction distortion affecting volume estimation and subtype.
links.quote: Defining passed registration for 3D spatial diagnosis as a Dice Similarity of >75% for intact tissue boundaries, 2.6% of WSIs are unqualified (Supplementary Information 3 ).

openai.sample_unit: whole-slide images, including 417 serial images from 70 prospective patients

links.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Three readers achieved absolute accuracy gains of 11.7%, 28.5%, and 28.5% on 137 WSIs. Prospectively, diagnostic accuracy improved from 82.86% to 92.9%; surgical approaches changed for 5 patients (among 70).
links.quote: Notably, HSFLA’s ROI suggestion feature reduced misdiagnosis rates by 11.7%, 28.5%, and 28.5% for the three pathologists, respectively.

links.outcome: Classification performance across internal and external hospital test sets
links.effect: Internal accuracy was 95.62% and AUC 98.71%; external accuracy was 91.7% and AUC 94.2% on 60 WSIs.
links.quote: In the three-classification task, it achieved a classification accuracy of 91.7% and an AUC of 94.2%.

links.outcome: Consecutive-slide registration failures associated with tissue damage and morphological distortion
links.effect: Using Dice Similarity of >75% for intact tissue boundaries as the passing criterion, 2.6% of WSIs failed registration quality requirements; reconstruction distortion affected invasive-volume estimation and subtype determination.
links.quote: Defining passed registration for 3D spatial diagnosis as a Dice Similarity of >75% for intact tissue boundaries, 2.6% of WSIs are unqualified (Supplementary Information 3 ).
